prompts.neutral:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: production raster sprite sheet for the MIST minimalist robot mouth, used for audio-synchronised speech.
Input image: previous mouth sheet is a style and character reference only. Redraw better mouth poses, preserve its abstract friendly cyan robot character.
Produce exactly 16 isolated mouth sprites in an invisible regular 4-column by 4-row grid on a perfectly flat pure white background. Square canvas. Equal square cells, no labels, no grid, no extra marks. Each cell contains ONLY a single mouth. Center horizontally in every cell. Keep one stable upper-mouth anchor at 46 percent of cell height: mouth opens downward from that line, never moves bodily upward as it opens. A relaxed mouth is 46 percent of a cell wide, maximum wide vowel 54 percent, big A height 26 percent. Keep all poses safely inside each cell.
Style: crisp smooth hand-drawn animation silhouette, confident rounded contours, a touch of deliberate organic asymmetry, but no wobble noise. One solid flat cyan #45E2DF, no gradients, no glow, no shadow, no highlights, no grain. Mouth openings are solid cyan silhouettes; closed lips are thick cyan curves or lines. Keep the drawing weight and geometric character consistent across all cells. Do not draw human lips, teeth, tongue, skin, face, eyes, noses or faces.
Exact order left-to-right then top-to-bottom:
Row 1: (1) REST: small relaxed shallow smile stroke with rounded caps, friendly but almost neutral. (2) MBP: closed pressed lips, clean straight horizontal rounded stroke, visibly closed. (3) RELEASE: a very narrow flat soft lozenge, just opening from MBP. (4) SMALL_AA: small rounded open mouth, the upper edge remains on the anchor and lower jaw drops slightly.
Row 2: (5) AA: fuller open speaking mouth; near-flat gently arced top, softly rounded lower jaw, taller than small_AA, never a dome rising upward. (6) EH: open horizontal softly squared oval with broad corners, middle height. (7) EE: widest shallow open smiling shape, clearly spread, not an enormous grin. (8) OH: tall narrow round vowel with nearly circular opening and rounded top.
Row 3: (9) OO: small pursed round vowel, narrower and shorter than OH. (10) FV: lower lip drawn slightly inward under a nearly flat upper edge, subtle off-center notch in top edge suggests a lip bite; narrow aperture, no teeth. (11) LNT: mid-small aperture with one tiny central indentation in top edge; distinct from round vowels but abstract, no tongue. (12) S: narrow shallow opening with a tiny visible central gap in silhouette, straighter and tenser than REST.
Row 4: (13) TH: shallow open mouth with tiny soft central downward protrusion on lower contour, no literal tongue. (14) WIDE_CLOSE: a halfway closing wide vowel, shallow narrow opening retaining the broad corners of EH/EE. (15) ROUND_CLOSE: a halfway closing rounded vowel, very small horizontally oval opening. (16) SMILE: settled friendly shallow smile stroke, slightly deeper than REST, same base width, not exaggerated.
Art direction: These are drawn speech shapes, not 16 variations of stretched circles. Maintain continuous character from rest to vowels. Distinguish closed, shallow, broad and rounded shapes clearly. NO multiple strokes outside the mouth, no cell numbers, NO decoration. Same cyan in every cel.

prompts.cleanup:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Clean up and consolidate these two generated robot mouth sheets. Input 1 is NEUTRAL; Input 2 is SMILE. Redraw them cleanly onto ONE OPAQUE PURE WHITE sheet with 4 columns and 8 rows. Use tall portrait canvas. Top four rows are all sixteen neutral mouths in their original order; bottom four rows are all sixteen smile mouths in their original order. All 32 cells equally sized. No separator, no heading, no labels, no grid.
Critical repair: Both source sheets have stray cyan speckles, dirty black rim artifacts, irregular jagged edges and partially transparent pixels around outlines. Remove ALL speckles, black outlines and stray pixels. Replace the whole background with solid opaque pure white (#FFFFFF). Absolutely NO alpha transparency. This is a printed contact sheet on white, not a transparent PNG asset. Each mouth must have smooth clean cyan-only antialiasing against WHITE. Solid flat cyan #45E2DF throughout, no texture, gradient, outline, glow or shadows.
Preserve the distinct mouth pose design, relative width, gently organic contour, and style from each source image. Only remove dirt and fix obvious roughness. Keep row3col2 / row7col2 FV narrow and slightly pinched rather than a big open smile. Keep row3col3 / row7col3 LNT medium open with tiny top indentation. Keep S in row3col4 / row7col4 a thin closed-looking horizontal aperture, remove its odd donut-shaped interior slit; it should be a shallow flat cyan lozenge.
Within each cell center the mouth horizontally. Fix the upper-mouth baseline to 44 percent of cell height and open lower jaws downward, never translate the entire mouth upward. All 32 mouths safely within their cells, equal generous margins. Closed strokes have consistent weight. No eyes, teeth, tongues, skin, lips or other facial parts.
Order within each set: REST, MBP, RELEASE, SMALL_AA / AA, EH, EE, OH / OO, FV, LNT, S / TH, WIDE_CLOSE, ROUND_CLOSE, SMILE. First set neutral, second set warm smile. Exactly 32 mouths, 4 by 8, OPAQUE WHITE background.

rejected.reason: Stray cyan pixels and dirty rims in transparent output.
Stray cyan pixels and dirty rims in transparent output.

oldFindings: FV and LNT were essentially open-smile variants, rather than distinct narrow consonant articulation.
Old AA dome appeared to expand above its baseline.
Old template loop advanced shapes without regard to what the audio said.
acceptedImprovements: AA and small_AA now open downwards from a shallow top edge, which gives lower-jaw motion.
Release, wide_close and round_close provide intermediate shapes for speech boundaries.
Clean contours and no visible isolated speckles in final sheet.
Sixteen poses per family, with matched intended scale and one reusable cyan style.
limitations: FV and LNT remain visually similar. Prefer release or S for a restrained FV in short speech, and reserve drawn FV for held or expressive use.
Neutral and smile families differ only subtly; this is useful for continuity but not a dramatic emotion change.
These are stylized robot visemes, not realistic anatomy or a phoneme recognizer.
Pixel colors retain small generated variations. A runtime solid-cyan tint can preserve the original silhouette while matching the rest of the face.
Artwork by itself does not synchronize speech. Audio playback timestamps must drive selection, silence and interruption must return to rest.

rest.note: Prefer the face's own mouth during long silence to keep expression identity.

MBP.note: Hold closure across the acoustic boundary; release to index 2 rather than jump directly to big A.

release.note: Small aperture between closed and open shapes.

AA.note: Reserve full opening for stressed or loud vowels.

EE.note: EH to EE is a natural diphthong sequence.

OO.note: OH to OO for rounding; OO to round_close near release.

S.note: Short and shallow; do not select solely because any noisy audio is present.

TH.note: Optional stylized pose; use small_AA if central protrusion is visually distracting.

SMILE.note: Expression accent, not a recurring speech phoneme.

playbackRecommendations.scheduler: Use actual playback clock plus returned alignment. Do not start mouths when text arrives before audio.
playbackRecommendations.coarticulation: Allow brief release/closing cels between large changes; keep consonant closure and stressed vowels prioritized at 8 fps.
playbackRecommendations.frequency: Update speech timing at display refresh even if eye animations use 8 fps. Do not quantize the voice clock to the eye rate.
playbackRecommendations.interruption: Stop mouth immediately on playback cancellation or generation change. Do not allow queued old visemes to resume.
playbackRecommendations.fallback: If only amplitude is available, use rest, release, small_AA and AA with smooth thresholds, explicitly not phoneme-accurate.
